Amazing !!!
Aug 2024 • Couples
What an amazing experience. My husband has been before and brought me back to celebrate our anniversary. 

The owner, Tracy recognized my husband and warmly welcomed him back. 

Located down an alley, a hidden gem, walk into a modern and unique atmosphere. French and Vietnamese fusion. Sits 5 tables, 2 levels, open kitchen with 3 detailed chefs. I had a seat that allowed me to view them at work. Watching them quietly work with perfect precision. I watched a dessert be replated 3 times before served, because it wasn’t perfect the first time. 

Tracy explained every wine pairings, the waiter explained in detail each dish and the presentation was amazing. 

The flavors of each dish exploded in my mouth and had me eagerly desiring the next dish. All for such a reasonable price. Easily would have paid $400 in America. Should be a Michelin rated restaurant.

Worst dining experience we had in central Vietnam. Avoid!
Dec 2023 • Couples
This is definitely the most disappointing “fine dining” experience I’ve ever had.

My wife and I were looking forward to this meal, marketed as a special one-of-a-kind experience. It was one-of-a-kind, but not in the way we expected.

This meal seems like it was constructed, from start to finish, for Instagram, rather than for our enjoyment. 

We arrived around 8 p.m. for our reservation and there were only two other tables occupied. We had no idea what to expect, in terms of food or service, but it turned out that both were seriously lacking.

Before I get into the details, I will say that our server staff, while poorly versed in English, were told to be kind and engaging. Unfortunately, they did not seem to understand anything were telling them as we were increasingly dissatisfied with our meal.

The dinner started out with a very pretty dinner roll that tasted like garlic bread. While the outside was Instagram-worthy, the inside was dry and unpleasant to eat. 

We waited 15 more minutes before the second course was served with a mediocre glass of sparking wine. I should say that the service staff had a routine of serving our course, then proceeded to describe the wine in broken English as our food got even colder in front of us. The timing was off the entire meal.

The used silverware and glassware were frequently left on the table until we requested they be cleared away. 

The second course, tiny shrimps, was also designed artistically, but the taste was bland and the consistency unpleasant. With each course, the silverware to consume it was delivered after the dish was placed, an unprofessional practice in a “fine dining” establishment.

The third course, an egg-yolk ravioli piece was decent, though it was ice cold when it was placed in front of us.

The moment when we realized that this meal was one of the worst we’ve had was when the server presented an attractive bun that she said was Beef Wellington, only the dish needed an additional 15 minutes to cook. How strange that they should show me a dish that wasn’t yet ready to serve. 

What’s more, my vegetarian wife was served a fish dish that was so bad, she left it with only a single bite nibble taken.

The wine accompaniments to our meal ranged from uninterested to terrible.

When finally the Wellington appeared, I was shocked that they said it was Wagyu beef. I’ve had Wagyu many times before and it was never this tough, stringy and difficult to chew. What’s more, they didn’t serve it with a steak knife, but rather a common dinner knife, and sawing through the dish, the elements of the Wellington all separated.

It reminded me of a bad episode of “Hell’s Kitchen.”

Dessert was not much better, with a trio of a little tart, a mushy macaron and some kind of cookie, along with a sugary gummy that looked like a marijuana leaf and tasted like children’s candy.

Most of this food seemed like it was prepared for photography and not for enjoyment.

They claimed the ingredients were high quality and expensive, but I suspect that is not the case based upon our tasting. For example, the "caviar" they used tasted mealy and without the snap I've experienced in fine dining restaurants in the past. 

We left early, disappointed beyond belief. 

When we read through these reviews in the Grab on the way home, we were alarmed to see that many people reported the owner threatened Vietnamese nationals for leaving bad reviews.

Well, we’re not Vietnamese, and we wanted to warn anyone who reads the positive reviews that this restaurant delivers bad food, unprofessional service, and disappointment at a high price point. 

And if the owner threatens honest reviewers, he should be reported to the tourist police.

We were told this would be a unique experience. It was, but not the in the way the promoters intended.

Definitely avoid!

Put this place on the map! (or don't)
Dec 2018 • Couples
A cosy little undiscovered fusion restaurant with 4 unremarkable tables outside a small kitchen. Pfft. However, it is very quickly distinguishable from most restaurants in this part of the world. 

The menu is limited but clear and extravagant. The chefs are darting around a pokey kitchen that wouldn't be fit for a few chickens. The end result is a masterpiece. We ate here on the two nights we stayed in da nang and felt like we were eating like royalty. The first night I had bangers and mash. The second a mouthwatering and amazingly cooked succulent stake. The best stake in town they claim- ok, I concur. 

Thanks so much and I regret to inform you will get busy if people continue to stumble across this place. With just 4 tables people might just end up being turned away because you're busy all the time.
